title: Variables
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Variables in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: What is a variable?
items.text: A variable is a name that refers to a value. It lets a program store and reuse data.

items.heading: Assignment
items.text: The = operator assigns the value on its right to the name on its left. It does not mean equality testing.

items.heading: Reassignment
items.text: A variable can be given a new value later. The same name can therefore refer to a different value.

items.heading: Variable names
items.text: Names should start with a letter or underscore and may contain letters, digits and underscores. They cannot start with a digit.

items.heading: Case sensitivity
items.text: Python variable names are case-sensitive. age, Age and AGE are different names.

items.heading: Storing text
items.text: A variable can refer to a string value.

items.heading: Storing numbers
items.text: Variables can also refer to integers, floats and other numeric values.

items.heading: Reusing data
items.text: Variables make it easy to use the same value in calculations or output without writing it again.

items.heading: Different value types
items.text: Python variables are dynamically typed, so a name can refer to values of different types at different times.

items.heading: Good naming
items.text: Meaningful names make code easier to understand. Prefer names such as total_price over unclear names such as x when the meaning matters.
